newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to tax-exempt extra sugar exports soon.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to tax-exempt extra sugar exports soon.

text.p: Brazil's government hopes to publish soon a decree exempting an additional 450,000 tonnes of sugar from export tax, a senior commodities official said.
But traders noted that most mills granted extra export quotas had already run out of sugar and the effect of the quota increase was likely to be limited.
Pedro Cabral, head of the sugar and alcohol department in Ministry of Industry and Commerce, said a decree authorizing the additional exports was published in December.
All that remained was for Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles to authorize the tax exemption.
"I hope the minister will make a decision soon so a decree exempting the exports from tax can be published, perhaps over the next few days," Cabral said.
In a decree published in the Official Journal Dec 19, the government raised the centre south's export quota by 400,000 tonnes and the north-northeast's by 52,318 tonnes.
That was in addition to 3.68 million tonnes and 1.522 million tonnes of exports allowed for the centre south and the north-northeast in the original 1996/97 sugar crop plan.
Traders said the increase was unlikely to result in a surge in physical shipments.
"Most of the mills who received extra quotas don't have any sugar to sell. So they are either going to sell their quotas (to other mills) or use it for the next crop," said one.

Traders expect total exports for the 1996/97 crop to be under 5.5 million tonnes, despite the extra quota, with the centre south accounting for about 4.0 million tonnes and the north-northeast for only about 1.4 million tonnes.
Centre south producers had pressed for additional exports because of higher evaluations of the crop size. North-northeast producers have concentrated on alcohol production.
